candidate_query.raw_sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(c.mrr) AS total_mrr, COUNT(o.id) AS order_cnt
FROM customers AS c
INNER JOIN orders AS o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.tenant_id = 'org_1' AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
GROUP BY c.id, c.name

violations_detected.title: Cartesian Metric Inflation: customers -> orders (Fanout: 20.0x)
violations_detected.message: Parent table "customers" measure "c.mrr" is aggregated (SUM) over 1:N join with "orders", inflating totals by approx 20.0x
violations_detected.remediation: Isolate child relation "orders" into a pre-aggregated Common Table Expression (CTE) before joining with "customers"
violations_detected.mathematical_proof: Phi_join(customers, orders) = 20.00 > 1.0. Aggregate SUM(c.mrr) evaluates across orders rows instead of 1 row per customers record.

rewritten_query.raw_sql:
WITH orders_agg AS (
SELECT customer_id AS customer_id, SUM(id) AS total_id
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(c.mrr) AS total_mrr, COUNT(o.id) AS order_cnt
FROM customers AS c
INNER JOIN orders_agg AS o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.tenant_id = 'org_1' AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
GROUP BY c.id, c.name

mutations_applied.description: Pre-aggregated child relation "orders" into CTE "orders_agg" on key "customer_id" to prevent 1:N Cartesian multiplication
